channel.title: The Federal Farmer on The Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in The Federal Farmer on The Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Farmer I
item.description: Warns that the new Constitution grants excessive power to the national government, threatening state sovereignty, individual liberties, and creating the potential for tyranny.

item.title: Farmer II
item.description: Argues that the proposed government will be too distant from the people, leading to poor representation and weakening accountability.

item.title: Farmer III
item.description: Expresses concern that the Constitution’s expansive powers over taxation, military control, and the potential for a standing army will lead to federal overreach.

item.title: Farmer IV
item.description: Critiques the proposed Senate, suggesting it will be an undemocratic body disconnected from the people, which could lead to a permanent, powerful elite.

item.title: Farmer V
item.description: Opposes the lack of a Bill of Rights, stressing that explicit protections for individual freedoms are necessary to prevent government abuse and ensure liberties.

item.title: Farmer VI
item.description: Questions the effectiveness of the Constitution’s checks and balances, arguing they will be inadequate in preventing abuses of power and protecting individual rights.

item.title: Farmer VII
item.description: Concerns about the centralization of power in the federal government and the lack of sufficient limits on federal authority, particularly regarding state rights and sovereignty.

item.title: Farmer VIII
item.description: Raises alarm over the creation of a standing federal army, fearing it could be used to suppress state governments and the will of the people.

item.title: Farmer IX
item.description: Criticizes the proposed executive branch for its potential to become overly powerful, undermining the balance of power and threatening republican principles.

item.title: Farmer X
item.description: Argues that the centralization of power in the federal government would weaken the authority of state governments and harm the rights and interests of local communities.

item.title: Farmer XI
item.description: Expresses concern that the new Constitution fails to adequately protect individual rights by not including a Bill of Rights, which could leave citizens vulnerable to abuse of power.

item.title: Farmer XII
item.description: Warns that the centralization of military and civil power will allow the federal government to override state authority, threatening local autonomy and governance.

item.title: Farmer XIII
item.description: Critiques the potential for the federal government’s centralization of authority to lead to a tyrannical system with unchecked power, eroding state governments and individual freedoms.

item.title: Farmer XIV
item.description: Argues that the lack of clear provisions for regular elections and term limits in the proposed system will lead to an entrenched political class and foster corruption.

item.title: Farmer XV
item.description: Suggests the new system would concentrate too much power in the Senate and executive, weakening the House of Representatives and creating an imbalance in government.

item.title: Farmer XVI
item.description: Warns that the broad powers granted to the federal government in the Constitution would lead to a dangerous concentration of power, diminishing state authority and individual freedoms.

item.title: Farmer XVII
item.description: Expresses concern that the federal government’s growing powers would undermine state governments, rendering them irrelevant and stripping citizens of local representation.

item.title: Farmer XVIII
item.description: Calls for the rejection of the Constitution, arguing it grants too much centralized power, lacks sufficient protections for individual rights, and could lead to governmental tyranny.
